plan.events.why: The plan's events are the two pasted drafts, and both come from the brief. The Terry plea exposes the dive-bar firing behind his 'nightlife curation' claim, and the hotel draft exposes the revolving door behind her 'strategic pause'. Each one pricks its owner's fear: being crooked and forgettable for him, being a clumsy anomaly for her. It stays at 4 because both events are self-inflicted misfires; no outside person or place presses in mid-chat, and nothing times them to the worst moment.

plan.events.raise: Have an outside party intrude at a pressure point, such as Terry replying or hotel HR calling her references just after she claims the pause was on her terms.

plan.setups.why: All three setups have a plant, a middle and an end. Clip, schedule and doors each come back, and the click ending pays the posture gear and the unscheduled hour. It clears the line, but the fall-apart ending pays only the door. The 'End' column also gives open questions ('what they do with their armor') rather than payoffs, so the schedule and clip are left unpaid in one ending.

plan.setups.raise: Give the fall-apart ending its own payoffs for the clip and the tattooed schedule, for example her filling his slot back in with a networking block.

plan.endings.why: The two endings are different stories. In one, both drop their armor and literally trade it; in the other, her list becomes a weapon and he politely escorts himself out. The click ending is tailored to this pair: undressing sitting down quietly pays off his nine-year standing-up shirt policy. The fall-apart ending is close to his Snap simply played out, which keeps it from a 6.

plan.endings.raise: Make the fall-apart ending turn on something only this pair could produce, such as both recognising the same mirror rehearsal and flinching from it.

plan.medium.why: The pastes and numbered audits work well in a chat. But both endings are staged as physical action in a shared room: undressing sitting down, and him holding a door open and walking out. A sample line also assumes sight with no photo mentioned. As written, a chat cannot carry these beats.

plan.voices.why: The voices differ on observable features. He writes full, ceremonial sentences with disclaimer openers and soft emoji. She uses 'hm.', numbered fragments and imperatives. Most sample lines can be attributed without names. His 'Understood.' could just as well be her clipped register, which keeps it from a 6.

plan.original.why: Underneath the size-contrast farce there are unpredicted turns. The climax is a swap of humiliating posture devices, and the intimacy is set sitting down. The collision is two mirrored defences, each reading the other's armor as rejection. It misses the strongest surprise in the brief: the two share near-identical histories (the replica app, the cropped portrait, mirror rehearsals), and the plan never lets them discover it.

plan.original.raise: Build a turn where they discover the matching replica-app or mirror-rehearsal secret, which would be both a surprise and the inevitable point of the night.

plan.format.why: The plan follows a consistent structure for both characters (Shows, Fear, Habit, Lie, Origin, Accident, Snap, Voice), then Collision, Setups, Endings and Heat, and it writes no chat exchange. It loses a point for having no short-game section. The voice samples and pastes are sample lines rather than scripted turns, so they stay within the structure.

plan.grounded.why: Most of the plan comes from the brief. The bodies follow the profile stats, the habits follow the texting traits, the dive-bar door and revolving-door heel are the night's truths, and the collarbone clip, horse-tack harness, yawn-bark and rosé are drawer items. 'Getting undressed sitting down' quietly uses Reuben's nipple policy, which is the kind of find a 5 needs. It stays at 4 because core material goes unused: his band-era test 'if they pass, the door actually opens', the arm wrestling in his bio, and both characters' stated safety needs. It also merges two of Brick's drawer items into 'three liters of boxed rosé in a towel'.

plan.contradictions.why: I found no fact that breaks the brief. The plan also handles two traps. The two backstories share several details, and the plan gives the cropped-portrait detail to Reuben only instead of duplicating it. It falls short of a 6 because these corrections are silent, and the rosé/towel merge slightly reworks two drawer facts.

plan.evaluation.why: The collision is a good mirrored misreading, and the click condition has each character drop the habit that wounds the other. But the plan never states either character's need: Reuben's 'stays present through pauses' and Brick's 'patient, exact, consistent' are absent. It names no test either, apart from implied lines like 'Say that again without the apology'. Fears and snaps stand in for the matrix, so Reuben has no test of Brick and most give-aways are orphans.

Swapping either character would break the doors setup and the gear-trade ending. It misses a 6 because the size-contrast heat opening is fairly generic for this app.

It is not a 5 because the plan never tracks who knows what. The harness propping her door appears in the ending without being planted, and the yawn-bark origin has no route to the chat.

plan.causal.why: The collision gives an engine, but the plan has no ordered beats. It is three parallel plant/middle/end setups plus two endings. Nothing says what makes Reuben admit the clip holds coffee, or what makes either accident happen. Most transitions read as 'and then'.

plan.guard.why: The moment exists and shows in the typing, because the markers vanish: 'Brick stops numbering' and 'Reuben drops the disclaimers'. What triggers it is missing. The only condition given is circular, 'when they drop the mirror-rehearsed lines', and nothing from tonight's events sets it off.

plan.guard.raise: Name the trigger, for example the twin door pastes landing, so that Brick laughing with him rather than at him is what stops her lists.

plan.heat.why: Heat opens on public anatomy, which suits this app, and escalation is gated on trust. The undressing comes only in the click ending, so nothing is fully explicit or logistical before the midpoint. It stays at 4 because there are only two steps, and the opening is already fairly blunt. No individual step is tied to a particular thing said.

plan.spread.why: The plant/middle/end structure spreads the three setups across the night, so the opening holds only plants and boasts. The accidents are never placed, though, and the doors middle needs both pastes at the same point, which risks clustering. There is no chartable rhythm and no reveal held back for late.

plan.spread.raise: Place each accident at a separate beat and hold one reveal, such as the curve-rehearsal habit, for the final third.

plan.collision.why: Both directions are named and drawn from both profiles: her numbered audits feed his fear of failing a physical inspection, and his exit clauses feed her fear of being a monstrous anomaly. The fall-apart ending runs on both habits, with her 1-2-3 audit and him holding the door and walking out. That puts it above the line. It stays at 4 because the collision is stated as a mechanism, not staged as a specific turn, and there is no planned escalation. Brick's Snap is also triggered by feeling "laughed at", not by his exit clauses, so the B-side direction never becomes a concrete moment.
